title: Colonial Rule: Case Studies from the Congo and Ghana
summary: Two case studies of colonial rule: King Leopold II's Congo Free State and the rubber trade, and the British conquest of the Asante kingdom in the Gold Coast.

notes.text: Case study 1: The Congo Free State

At the Berlin Conference, King **Leopold II of Belgium** was given the huge **Congo Free State** (about 80 times the size of Belgium) as his **personal property**, not as a Belgian colony. He promised to end the slave trade and bring 'civilisation', but he ran the Congo to make money for himself.

In the 1890s the invention of the inflatable bicycle and car tyre created an enormous demand for **rubber**. Wild rubber vines grew in the Congo's rainforests. Leopold's agents and companies forced Congolese people to collect it.

items: Each village was given a **quota** of rubber to collect. People had to go deep into the forest for weeks.
Women and children were taken **hostage** until the men returned with enough rubber.
The **Force Publique**, Leopold's army, punished villages that failed to meet quotas by burning homes, flogging with the *chicotte* (a hippo-hide whip) and killing people.
Soldiers had to prove they had not wasted bullets by bringing back the **severed hands** of those they had killed; hands were also cut off the living.
Farming was neglected, causing famine and disease. Historians estimate that the population fell by **millions** between 1885 and 1908.

notes.title: Source C: Congolese testimony (a composite based on accounts collected by missionaries and Roger Casement, about 1903–1904)
notes.text: We were always in the forest looking for rubber, going without food. Our wives had to give up working in the gardens and fields. Then we starved. When we failed and our rubber was short, the soldiers came to our towns and killed us.

notes.title: Writing a cause-and-effect answer
notes.problem: Explain why Leopold II's rule in the Congo was so violent.
steps: Start with the aim: the Congo was his personal property and was run for profit from rubber and ivory.
Give the method: villages were set quotas of rubber to collect.
Give the result: failure to meet quotas was punished with hostage-taking, mutilation and killing.
notes.answer: Violence was built in, because profit depended on forcing people to meet quotas.

notes.text: Missionaries, the journalist **E. D. Morel** and the British diplomat **Roger Casement** exposed the abuses. Photographs of mutilated children shocked the world. In **1908** the Belgian government took the Congo away from Leopold and it became the **Belgian Congo**. Conditions improved somewhat, but Belgium continued to exploit the colony until independence in **1960**.
Case study 2: The Asante and the Gold Coast

The **Asante** (Ashanti) kingdom in present-day **Ghana** was a powerful, wealthy state, rich in gold and controlling trade routes. Its capital was **Kumasi** and its ruler the **Asantehene**. The **Golden Stool** was the sacred symbol of the unity and soul of the Asante nation.

rows: Several Anglo-Asante wars; British forces burned Kumasi in 1874
Britain occupied Kumasi and exiled the Asantehene, Prempeh I, to the Seychelles
The British governor demanded to sit on the Golden Stool. **Yaa Asantewaa**, the Queen Mother of Ejisu, led an uprising (the War of the Golden Stool)
The uprising was defeated; Asante was annexed into the British Gold Coast colony
The Gold Coast became independent as **Ghana**, the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence, led by Kwame Nkrumah

notes.text: The British never captured the Golden Stool, which had been hidden. Under British rule, the Gold Coast became a major producer of **cocoa**, gold and timber for export, but most of the profits went to Britain.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: When comparing case studies, consider: who ruled, what resources were wanted, how labour was obtained, how people resisted, and the long-term effects.

notes.title: Comparing resistance
notes.problem: Name one way the Asante's experience of colonial rule shows that Africans resisted it.
steps: Identify an event: the war of 1900, led by Queen Mother Yaa Asantewaa.
Say why it happened: the British governor demanded the Golden Stool, the sacred symbol of the Asante nation.
Say what it shows: Africans fought to defend their independence and identity.
notes.answer: The Asante fought the British in 1900 to protect the Golden Stool.

(b) ✓ Soldiers killed them (1)

questions.prompt: Describe THREE methods used to force Congolese people to collect rubber.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): quotas; taking women and children hostage; flogging with the chicotte; burning villages; killing; cutting off hands

questions.prompt: Give ONE similarity between colonial rule in the Congo and in the Gold Coast.
questions.memo: ✓✓ Any valid similarity explained, e.g. both were ruled by Europeans to take resources (rubber / gold, cocoa) and the profits went to Europe; in both, Africans resisted and were defeated by force
